          Newcastle vs Aston Villa Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 16, 2026
          
                      Chirag Sharatkumar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After a scintillating Champions League win in midweek, Unai Emery’s side will look to carry their momentum into domestic action. We look ahead to Saturday's Premier League clash with our Newcastle United vs Aston Villa prediction and preview.

After picking up hugely contrasting results in their last respective outings, Newcastle and Aston Villa meet in the Premier League on Saturday, with both sides looking to improve their domestic performances after inconsistent starts.

Matthias Jaissle’s side fell to a 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Frank Lampard’s Coventry City on Monday, with Sidiki Cherif, Ellis Simms, and Stephen Mfuni striking in the second half to seal victory after Jack Rudoni’s sixth-minute penalty.
Sven Botman netted a second-half consolation, but that will have meant precious little to Jaissle, whose biggest challenge at present is surely plugging his side’s leaky defence.

The Magpies have conceded 13 Premier League goals this season – their third-highest total after six matches, behind only 1999-00 (18) and 2021-22 (14). They went on to finish 11th in both of those campaigns.

Beyond the goals, though, Jaissle will be further concerned by how many shots his team have allowed. Newcastle have faced 34 shots on target this season, with only Chelsea (36) facing more in the competition.

It has been an especially concerning issue at home, with the Magpies now going 12 Premier League matches without a clean sheet at St. James’ Park. They last endured a longer run between December 1998 and August 1999 under Ruud Gullit (13 games).

Perhaps most worrying for Jaissle is that only Tottenham (13) have lost more Premier League games in 2026 than Newcastle’s 12, while the Magpies have conceded the joint-most goals in the competition this year (44, level with Chelsea).
Aston Villa, meanwhile, will be riding the high of yet another spectacular European performance.
Unai Emery’s side thrashed Fenerbahce 6-0 in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both netting braces alongside goals from Johan Manzambi and Tammy Abraham.
While that victory has lifted them towards the upper reaches of the Champions League standings, the Villans’ domestic form tells a different story.
They sit 16th in the table with just six points and have won just one of their six matches so far, squandering a late lead against Brentford last time out to eventually settle for a 2-2 draw.
Like Newcastle, Villa have faced similar, though perhaps not quite as extreme, defensive struggles this season.
They have shipped 11 goals across six Premier League matches so far – their most at this stage of a season since 1986-87 (16), when they eventually finished bottom of the table.
The Villans have also faced an uncharacteristic 15.8 shots per game this season – their most since the 2019-20 season, when they allowed an average of 16 per game.
Still, faith in Emery to guide Villa up the table will remain high, especially with the Spaniard on the cusp of recording his 100th Premier League victory.
He has won 99 of his 196 matches in the competition (D44 L53), and victory over Newcastle would make him the joint-ninth-fastest manager to reach 100 Premier League wins.
Villa will, however, have to be wary of Harvey Barnes, who has become a constant thorn in their side in recent times.

The Newcastle winger has contributed to 10 goals in 13 Premier League matches against Villa (six goals, four assists) – his joint-most against a single opponent along with West Ham. He has only found the net more against Leeds United (seven goals).
Villa, meanwhile, will hope Jackson can build on his recent good form.
